title: Advice one: study mathematics
summary: Thomas tells young musicians math is a perfect science that teaches thinking and that music is basically math.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I want to ask you this, Foots. We had said that if you had some advice to give to some young people, you want to talk to young people and give them some advice about living and about music and carrying themselves in music... What advice would you give them, Foots?

Well, Milt, the only thing I can think of is some of the things I feel that helped me so much. Now, this first thing I want to talk about, it may be too late for some guys to study Math, but I'll mention it anyway.
Well, there are some guys from college who pick this up...
What's in Math, Foots? What do you consider Math?

Well, Math is one of the greatest...one of the most perfect sciences that there is. And it applies to almost everything you get into. I remember, I took Economics, and Economics dwells on Math. And when I got into music, I later on found out that music ain't nothin' but Math.
Well, it's more or less a discipline, isn't it?
It's a discipline. Everything has to be disciplined. You have to be (?).

And one of the most important things I got out of Math is, one day our Math teacher told the class, he said, "Later on in life, you may never use all these intricate problems and whatnot. But the one important thing that Math does, it teaches you to think." And you know, thinking is one of the greatest things that we need to do. We all have that quality, and we need to use it. Because if you think it out, and it don't make sense, you don't use it! But if you use it and it makes sense, keep using it. And I know I got into so many situations, that's why I wanted to bring up that little thing about Math -- because I think it's so important.
So your suggestion is to study some form of Math, huh?

Yeah, if you haven't got to that point. Study Math. Don't get into it and don't like it... And if you get the fundamentals of Math, you've got it. If you've get fractions... Well, number one, the first thing you get is addition and multiplication and division, and then if you can get fractions, you've got the basic foundation for Math. All the other subjects you get involved with, you will go back and dwell on that principal thing. And it so happened
with me I just got crazy about it, and majored in it.
